title: Improbable Destinies: Fate, Chance, and the Future of Evolution
author: Jonathan B. Losos
note: Selected on positive reader reception, praise from David Quammen and Carl Zimmer, and Nature's best-books recognition. Explanatory experimental science rather than specialist training. Ecology and organism-environment interactions predominate enough for T11=-10; T12=0. Experimental comparisons, contingency and uncertainty are central: this is not an unsupported sweeping evolutionary narrative. No serious veto established. The book weighs convergence against historical contingency rather than claiming complete predictive control.
notes: Field and laboratory experiments are distinguished from larger extrapolations; alternative outcomes and unresolved questions are explicit.
Links genetics, organisms, environments and experimental design; limited economic or institutional integration.
Good transfer to reasoning about replication, path dependence and prediction limits.
Explains selection and contingent trajectories through interventions and comparisons.

D=8, moderate confidence from the author-hosted Nebraska-mice excerpt, professional reviews and reader reports. Different experimental settings add mechanisms and boundary conditions; some reviewers find later study detail slow.
Experimental reasoning and contingency remain durable.
Useful scientific modeling and inference, less direct technology or industrial fit.
Leading experimental evolutionary biologist; extensive specialist research underlies the synthesis.
Clear organizing question connects distinct investigations.
Accessible explanations generally preserve uncertainty.

title: Projections: A Story of Human Emotions
author: Karl Deisseroth
note: Selected on named neuroscience expert praise, professional reviews and positive reader response, with substantial reader dissent about style retained. Clinical cases and neuroscience explanation are the main purpose, not health advice or emotional support; V7 is not established. It is literary nonfiction rather than fiction or a technical clinical curriculum. Author-described imaginative reconstruction must not be confused with verbatim patient testimony. Disease and psychiatric disorders dominate, T11=-10. Neuroscience rather than philosophy is central, T12=0. No high-confidence foundational veto established; evolutionary suggestions are less secure than circuit findings.
notes: Clinical experience and established research support the account, but reconstructed inner states and evolutionary speculation limit inference.
Connects circuits, behavior, psychiatric practice and experience, with little industry or institutional analysis.
Some useful distinctions about mechanisms and observation, less strategic transfer outside science.
Optogenetic intervention supports causal understanding; literary cases do not independently prove mechanisms.

D=6.5, moderate confidence from professional reviews, author explanation and contrasting reader reports. Cases add distinct disorders and perspectives; metaphors and introspection can delay scientific content. No complete-text audit.
The clinical-scientific perspective endures, though current research details will develop.
Technology for probing neural circuits fits; disease-centered narrative reduces direct preference fit through T11.
Major investigator and clinician with named expert recognition, distinct from proof of every speculative claim.
Case structure is memorable for many readers, while others find the scientific thread interrupted.
Ambitious literary language sometimes obscures rather than sharpens concepts.
